correctness.rationale: For m>=4, the k=1 and k=2 real normalized Fourier pairs give universal two-mode upper bound λ2≤min(D_m a_bar+2b_bar,A_m a_bar) for any independently weighted design. Uniform orbit rates attain this bound because their full Fourier spectrum has first odd and first nonzero even minima. With 2m a+mcb=B, maximizing the minimum of two affine functions yields positive-chord intersection if c<4/D_m, a whole segment at equality, rim-only if c>4/D_m. Equality in the first Fourier pair forces its cos/sin into the λ2 eigenspace; the complex equation sin(π/m)(a_(j−1)−a_j)=0 forces all rim rates equal and real parts all antipodal rates equal. Hence unrestricted optimizer rigidity holds. Taylor D~π²/m² and A~4π²/m² establishes O(m^-2) chord spending and fourfold spectral gain. Independent eigenspectra for m=4,5,7 across sub/supercritical prices agree; finite tests are not all-m proof.
